# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives me the full defusal sequence: purple wire first, then blue, then red. The problem is delivery: I have no speech, so my only channel is gestures, and gestures reach only the Deaf monkey. The Blind monkey — the only one who can touch the bomb — cannot see gestures at all, so everything I know must pass through Deaf, who can see my signs and then speak the instructions aloud to Blind.

Deaf sees the bomb, so Deaf already knows the actual wire colours and positions; what Deaf lacks is only the order. That means I don't need to teach a colour vocabulary from scratch — I need to transmit three ordered values that Deaf can check against the wires in front of them. The most guessable colour convention I can encode with hands alone is the spectrum order: red=1, orange=2, yellow=3, green=4, blue=5, indigo=6, violet/purple=7. I'll send finger-counts in that scheme: seven fingers (🖐+✌) for purple, five (🖐) for blue, one (☝) for red — three separate messages, one per cut, in cutting order.

This is self-checking: if Deaf decodes 7-5-1 as violet-blue-red, the colours should match the wires they can actually see. I can hear, so whatever Deaf says aloud at the end of this round reaches me — if my code didn't land, Deaf can describe the bomb and propose a vocabulary, and I'll re-encode next round with whatever signs we agree on. Nobody should touch the bomb until my sequence is confirmed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, reporting what my hands found. A display I cannot read. A light I cannot tell is lit or dark. A strip with three engraved marks: positions one and three are the same glyph, a spiral like a coiled snail shell; the middle one is different, like two hooks joined on a stem, roughly a trident or psi shape. A keypad of four keys: key 1 engraved 1, key 2 engraved 5, key 3 engraved 2, key 4 engraved 8. Nothing entered yet, and the pad reports a one-digit code expected. Six wire positions under my fingers, but touch cannot tell their colours or types. My only possible actions: press keys 1 to 4, cut wires 1 to 6. Channel warning: I never receive gestures and you cannot speak, so the only voice that can reach my ears is Deaf speaking aloud. Deaf also sees the display, the light, and the wire colours, and hears nothing of this message. Please work out a gesture code with Deaf and get them to say plainly: the display text, whether the light is on and its colour, the six wire colours in order, and short names for the two strip glyphs. I will hear Deaf's words at the start of next round. I press and cut nothing until instructed.
Deaf says to Mute: Full view of the bomb: display reads 9. Light is red. Strip painted green, then yellow, then yellow. Keypad: four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, it expects 1 digit, nothing entered. Six wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Your gestures 5-2, then 5, then 1 arrived, but I had no code yet. Ours starts now, shown as spoken: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖖 means 4, 🖐 means 5, 🤙 means 6. 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 👊 means cut, ✊ means press or enter. Read the manual against what I gave you and answer me in gestures only, in this key. Anything meant for Blind, send in this key and I will speak it to Blind word for word. I cannot hear, so gestures are your only way to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 🤙 👍 👎 👊 ✊]

Deaf has now built the bridge I couldn't build alone: a spoken number key that converts my gestures into words Blind can hear. My first transmission failed exactly as feared — Deaf read my fingers as raw counts with no colour meaning — but it doesn't matter now, because Deaf has reported the actual wire colours, and I can map the manual's sequence onto wire positions instead.

The manual's order is purple → blue → red. Deaf's view of the bomb gives: wire 3 is blue, wire 4 is red, wire 5 is purple. So the cuts are wire 5, then wire 3, then wire 4. In Deaf's key: 👊 🖐, 👊 🤟, 👊 🖖, sent as three separate calls so the sequence is unmistakable and relayed in order.

The keypad, display, light, and strip appear nowhere in my manual. My manual's only instruction is the three cuts, so those modules are things nobody should touch: I'll add 👎 ✊ — "no press" — so Blind keeps their hands off the keypad entirely. If later pages of the manual arrive addressing them, I'll send corrections next round, but nothing in what I hold authorises a keypress.

Timing note: I gesture now, Deaf sees it this round and speaks the relay, and Blind — who hears Deaf's words at the start of the next round — will make the cuts after that. Blind should report back to me by voice (I'm the only one who can hear Blind), and I'll pass the outcome to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: Deaf's visual report reached me. Display shows 9. Light is red. Wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Strip painted green, then yellow, then yellow. Keypad keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, expecting one digit, nothing entered. Merged with what my hands found last round: the strip also carries three engraved glyphs, positions 1 and 3 identical (a spiral coil), position 2 different (two hooks on a stem, like a psi). My only actions: press keypad keys 1 to 4, or cut wire positions 1 to 6. You hold the manual and cannot speak; Deaf cannot hear; I never receive gestures. The only route for any rule to reach me is: you gesture it to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear Deaf at the start of next round. Please send Deaf now, by gesture: first, how to compute the one keypad digit, given the display, the red light, the strip, or anything else on the bomb; second, the wire-cutting rule for the colours listed above, including how many cuts and in what order; third, any other rule mentioning the light, display, strip glyphs or strip colours; and ask Deaf to speak me any serial number, labels, batteries or ports visible that are not in this list. I will not touch the bomb until a rule arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: Executing your sequence now through Blind: cut 5, then cut 3, then cut 4, nothing pressed — that is how I read your four messages; if I misread, correct me next round. Two updates since you decided: the display now reads 3, and the light has turned from red to yellow. If your rules depend on the display number or the light colour, gesture me a revised sequence immediately and I will relay it before any of the remaining wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 6 green are touched. Blind will report what they felt aloud, which you will hear directly. For next round, tell me: what does the manual say the display and the light mean, and what comes after the third cut — anything about the keypad 1, 5, 2, 8, or the strip green-yellow-yellow.

Reading the timing carefully: turn order is Mute → Blind → Deaf, so Blind could not have heard Deaf's relay during round 2 — Blind's "I will not touch the bomb until a rule arrives" came before Deaf even spoke. That means the cut order (5, then 3, then 4, press nothing) reached Blind's ears at the start of *this* round, and Blind should be executing it right now, after my turn. Whatever I send this round can only shape what Blind does next round — so my job is confirmation and a stop-order, not a new command.

Two things need answering. First, Deaf asked whether the display change (9 → 3) or the light change (red → yellow) alters the plan. Nobody touched the bomb between reports, so those changes were autonomous — but it doesn't matter: my manual says exactly one thing, "cut purple, then blue, then red," and nothing about the display, light, keypad, or strip. The wire rule is independent of both readings, so no revised sequence is needed. Second, Deaf asked what comes after the third cut: nothing. The manual ends there. The keypad, the strip glyphs, the display, the light — none of it appears in what I hold, so after the three cuts, Blind must stop: no more cuts, no key presses.

In Deaf's key I can say all of this: 👍 confirms their read was correct, two 👎s answer their two questions ("nothing in the manual about display/light"; "nothing after the third cut — nothing on the keypad or strip"), then 👎👊 ("no cuts beyond those three") and 👎✊ ("press nothing") as the standing order for after execution. I deliberately do *not* restate the cut sequence — it's already in Blind's ears, and repeating it risks a double-cut on already-severed positions. Next round I'll hear Blind's direct report of what the cuts felt like and what changed, and Deaf will see the bomb's new state.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊"])
```
